motivation: Return fragility shows that exact points re-recording Thalassia after a one-year loss are more likely to be unrecorded again than continuously occupied points. Test whether the return state is also quantitatively depressed at the moment of re-recording.

source.group_state_builder: same point-year Thalassia presence logic used by analysis/33_community_buffering.py and analysis/42_return_fragility.py
source.quantitative_measurement: numeric Thalassia Braun-Blanquet measurement from pinned eMoF

three_year_sequence.years: t, t+1, t+2 observed consecutively at the same stable meter mark
three_year_sequence.recovered_group: Thalassia present at t, absent at t+1, present at t+2
three_year_sequence.continuous_group: Thalassia present at t, t+1, and t+2
three_year_sequence.quantitative_requirement: numeric point-level Braun-Blanquet state observed at both t and t+2
three_year_sequence.point_year_quantitative_rule: mean all numeric focal Braun-Blanquet measurements assigned to the exact point-year; if focal presence is recorded but no numeric Braun-Blanquet exists, point-year is missing for this endpoint

primary_hypothesis.statement: At the return year, recovered points have lower Thalassia Braun-Blanquet state than continuously occupied points after stable-transect identity, return year, and source-year point Braun-Blanquet state are represented.
primary_hypothesis.estimator: standardized recovered_group coefficient; negative means recovery debt
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: upper bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for recovered_group coefficient < 0

secondary: raw target Braun-Blanquet mean/median in recovered and continuous groups

interpretation.supported: Re-recorded Thalassia returns in a quantitatively depressed state relative to uninterrupted occupancy, consistent with recovery debt or hysteresis at annual resolution.
interpretation.unsupported: Re-recorded points are not detectably lower in exact-point Braun-Blanquet state than uninterrupted controls after baseline state, site, and year adjustment; binary return fragility is not accompanied by the tested quantitative recovery debt.

claim_boundary: Braun-Blanquet is an ordinal abundance state, not percent cover or biomass.
A negative recovered-group coefficient is consistent with recovery debt but does not identify residual stress, rhizome state, detectability, or demographic mechanism.
Continuous controls are observational and adjusted for stable node, return year, and source point abundance; they are not experimentally matched.
Return is recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not proven genet-level recolonization.
Do not change sequence patterns, period, quantitative inclusion rule, control variables, minima, learner, or support threshold after opening target quantitative states.
